title: The Secret Homecoming
premise: Petra Joubert arrives at Hollowmere Academy as the new kid with a chip on his shoulder and a talent for pretending everything is fine. When his first real friend, Wren, vanishes leaving only a brass ring of keys, Petra discovers the school was built over a sealed underground wing where generations of 'missing' students were quietly erased. To open the sealed door he must win both the swimming championship everyone watches and the secret Trial of Keys no one admits exists — because only a champion's keys turn the lock. He wins the race that doesn't matter, loses the one that does by seconds, and finds another way in: Wren is alive below, and freeing her means exposing the school's beloved founders and choosing truth over the found family that finally took him in.
about_author: Sebastian Blackwood is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent years listening to students' rumors about what lay beneath their campus. He writes YA mysteries about kids who refuse to accept the official story.

chapters.title: The New Kid Math
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Arriving mid-term at Hollowmere Academy, Petra calculates exactly how invisible he needs to be to survive senior year. A girl named Wren dismantles his strategy in one lunch period by simply refusing to leave him alone. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness cracked open by unexpected warmth.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra settles into routines: swim team tryouts, dorm life, Wren dragging him across every corridor of the school. She keeps asking odd questions about the east wing's bricked-up archway. Emotional beat: belonging arriving so easily it feels suspicious.

chapters.title: The Ring of Brass
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (final entry). Wren records her last night: she has copied seven old keys from the archives and believes the founders' ledger hides a sealed wing. She hears something breathing behind the east wall. Emotional beat: brave curiosity tipping into dread.

chapters.title: Empty Bed
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Wren misses morning practice — impossible. Her room is untouched except for a brass keyring on her pillow, seven keys, one warm to the touch. The headmaster calls her departure 'a family matter.' Emotional beat: disbelief hardening into refusal.

chapters.title: Official Story
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Adults close ranks: counselors, the headmaster, even kind Coach Adeyemi repeat identical phrases. Petra notices the phrase 'family matter' appears verbatim in a fifty-year-old yearbook about another missing student. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the lie is institutional.

chapters.title: Seven Locks
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra and Wren's roommate, Dev, test the keys against doors across campus; six fit nothing, but the seventh fits a maintenance hatch behind the pool. Below it: stairs going down into dark. Emotional beat: fear converted into mission.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, an archive nerd, decodes the founders' ledger: every few decades a student 'transfers' and never arrives anywhere. The sealed wing is called the Undercroft, and the ledger says only 'a champion's keys may turn the lock.' Emotional beat: scholarly awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Trials of the Season
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Swim season begins in earnest; Petra qualifies for regionals, discovering the championship matters more than sport — champions get ceremonial keys at Founders' Day. Emotional beat: ambition with a hidden, desperate purpose.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's dorm is searched; his notebook on the keys goes missing. A warning note appears in his locker: SOME DOORS ARE LOCKED FOR YOU. Emotional beat: paranoia, and the first sense he could be next.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Breathing
chapters.summary: Petra and Dev's alternating POV. They descend the maintenance stairs at night and reach a second door — iron, seven keyholes. From behind it, faintly: tapping, rhythmic, deliberate. Three taps. Wren's signal from their first friendship pact. Emotional beat: terror and joy colliding.

chapters.title: Allies and Liars
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra recruits swim teammate Ines, who reveals her aunt was a Hollowmere 'transfer' decades ago. But Coach Adeyemi catches them with the ledger — and instead of reporting them, says quietly: 'Not here. Not yet.' Emotional beat: trust extended cautiously into the adult world.

chapters.title: What the School Protects
chapters.summary: Coach Adeyemi's POV. Flashback chapter: thirty years ago, Adeyemi found the Undercroft as a student, was threatened into silence, and watched his best friend become a 'transfer.' He stayed to guard the door from inside the system. Emotional beat: guilt, complicity, and long-deferred courage.

chapters.title: Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Regionals: Petra wins the 200 free in a personal best, earning his ceremonial champion's key — and realizes mid-podium that the crowd's roar means nothing compared to three taps behind iron. Emotional beat: hollow triumph sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The real trial: the seven keys must each be earned through acts tied to the founders' virtues — honesty, sacrifice, loyalty. Petra already holds two without knowing; the third requires confessing publicly why he transferred schools. Emotional beat: vulnerability as literal currency.

chapters.title: Confession at Assembly
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At Founders' assembly, Petra abandons his speech and tells the whole school about Wren, the keys, the tapping. Half laugh; half go pale. The headmaster's smile doesn't move. Emotional beat: exposure — relief and danger at once.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: Petra and Dev's POV. Retaliation is swift: Petra is suspended, the hatch welded, Dev's archive access revoked. But Ines photographs the welding crew — including the headmaster himself, after hours. Emotional beat: despair met with evidence.

chapters.title: The Sixth Key
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines tracks down the retired groundskeeper who poured the concrete in 1989; he gives her the sixth key and a confession recorded on cassette. The seventh key, he warns, belongs to whoever loves the missing most. Emotional beat: grief transformed into ammunition.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fractured
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The group fractures: Dev wants to go public first, Ines wants police, Petra wants the door now because the tapping has stopped. A bitter fight ends with Dev walking out. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against urgency and truth.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Founders' Day night, Petra uses his champion's key and six others at the iron door — six locks turn, the seventh sticks. Behind him, Dev returns holding the keyring Wren left: 'She left them to you. You're the one who loves her most.' The door opens. Emotional beat: the found family reassembling at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Inside: not monsters but a hidden dormitory where inconvenient students were isolated and 're-enrolled' elsewhere — and Wren, who escaped her room and has survived weeks in the tunnels, waiting by the door she couldn't unlock alone. They climb out into torchlight and a crowd. Emotional beat: reunion, rage, and witness.

chapters.title: Truth or Belonging
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Climax: the headmaster offers Petra a deal — silence, reinstatement, a future — before the assembled trustees. Petra chooses truth, plays the cassette, shows the photos. The school's myth collapses; Coach Adeyemi steps forward as witness. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid willingly.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue tone. Weeks later: investigations begin, Wren recovers surrounded by people who refused to stop looking, and Petra — no longer the new kid — hangs the seven keys above his desk. Belonging, he finally understands, isn't given by institutions; it's built by who shows up. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
